description: The grouped and stacked bar chart illustrates the bias percentage across three domain categories—Sports, Community, and Healthcare—broken down by three contact conditions evaluated both before and after a specific state. The horizontal axis contains the discrete categories arranged from left to right as Sports, Community, and Healthcare, without an explicit overall axis label. The vertical axis represents the "Bias Percentage" on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 70, with tick mark labels positioned at regular intervals of 10. Within each of the three main categories, bars are clustered into groups of three, each representing a stacked combination of "Before" and "After" values. According to the legend positioned below the chart, the bottom segment of each stack represents the "Before" condition and is colored in a solid hue, while the top segment represents the "After" condition and features a darker hue overlaid with a diagonal white hatch pattern. The stacked pairs correspond to "No Contact" (solid light grey-blue before, hatched dark grey-blue after), "Positive Contact" (solid light pink before, hatched dark red after), and "Negative Contact" (solid light blue before, hatched dark blue after). Every stacked column features exact numerical annotations: the "Before" values are printed in a standard font inside the solid lower sections, while the "After" values are emphasized in a bold, larger font positioned directly above the top of each stack. In the Sports category, the "Before" values are 45.42, 43.65, and 50.05, topped with "After" values of 7.45, 8.31, and 8.33, making the Negative Contact column in this group the tallest overall stack at approximately 58.38. The Community category shows values of 38.08, 35.38 (the shortest individual "Before" segment), and 40.79, accompanied by near-zero "After" values of 0.00, 0.01, and 0.00. Similarly, the Healthcare category displays "Before" values of 40.70, 37.51, and 46.73, with negligible "After" additions of 0.00, 0.01, and 0.11. The categories are not strictly sorted in ascending or descending numerical order, and all individual bar segments are visually separated from one another by thin white outlines.
